problem_statement: The employee directory table on the payroll dashboard currently displays all employees with no way to narrow the list. As the number of employees grows, managers and HR administrators need a quick way to locate specific people by name or job title without scrolling through the entire roster. A real-time search box will allow users to filter employees instantly as they type, improving usability without requiring a page reload.

user_stories.i_want: to type in a search box and see the employee table filter instantly
user_stories.so_that: I can find a specific employee quickly without scrolling through the full roster

user_stories.i_want: to search by partial name or partial title
user_stories.so_that: I don't need to remember the exact spelling to locate a record

user_stories.i_want: to clear the search and return to the full employee list
user_stories.so_that: I can easily reset my view after finding what I need

user_stories.i_want: to see a clear indication when no employees match my search
user_stories.so_that: I know the directory was searched and no results were found rather than assuming the page failed to load

must_have: A search input field displayed above the employee directory table on the main dashboard
Real-time filtering of the employee table rows as the user types (client-side, no page reload required)
Filtering applies to both the employee name and job title columns simultaneously
Search is case-insensitive so that 'CEO' and 'ceo' both match 'Chief Executive Officer'
An empty-state message is shown in the table body when no rows match the current search term
Clearing the search input restores all employee rows
should_have: A visible label or placeholder text on the search input that communicates both name and title are searchable (e.g., 'Search by name or title…')
The search input is accessible with a proper <label> element associated via for/id attributes
The employee count or a result count is updated to reflect how many employees match the current filter
Search state is not persisted across page reloads (stateless client-side only)
nice_to_have: A clear/reset button (×) inside the search input to dismiss the filter in one click
Debounced input handling to avoid excessive DOM manipulation on rapid keystrokes
Matching text within the name or title cell is visually highlighted

acceptance_criteria: Verify a search input element is present above the employee directory table on the dashboard (GET /)
Verify typing a partial employee name into the search box hides rows that do not match and keeps rows that do match, without a page reload
Verify typing a partial job title into the search box hides rows that do not match and keeps rows that do match, without a page reload
Verify the search is case-insensitive (e.g., typing 'ceo' matches an employee with title 'Chief Executive Officer')
Verify that when the search term matches no employees, a message such as 'No employees match your search' appears in the table
Verify clearing the search input (emptying the text field) restores all employee rows
Verify the search input has an accessible label (either a visible <label> or aria-label attribute)
Verify the feature does not break existing CRUD operations (add, edit, delete employee) present on the dashboard
out_of_scope: Server-side search or filtering via query parameters
Filtering by columns other than name and title (e.g., salary, manager, home address)
Persisting the search term across page loads or in browser history
A dedicated search results page or route
Full-text search across all employee data fields
Adding new filterable columns or sorting capabilities
Authentication or permission checks for accessing the search feature
open_questions: Should the search box filter both the summary table (Employee directory) AND the expandable edit cards below it, or only the summary table?
Should the result count display (e.g., 'Showing 3 of 6 employees') be added to the panel heading, or is simply hiding rows sufficient?
Should the empty-state message replace all table rows, or should the table header remain visible with only an empty body?
